labels.running:
Malignant hyperthermia
Choose another scenario
A fit 35-year-old man, induced with propofol and succinylcholine and maintained on sevoflurane 2 %. The jaw is stiff after the succinylcholine. Minutes into surgery the EtCO₂ climbs at the same ventilation and the heart rate rises; untreated, the core temperature passes 38.5 °C about 19 minutes after induction and he arrests in VF at 42 °C about 45 minutes after induction. Run the MH crisis: trigger off, oxygen, hyperventilation, dantrolene, cooling and the potassium.
Induced: propofol, succinylcholine 1.5 mg/kg (masseter rigidity), intubated; sevoflurane 2 %
Surgery under way: sevoflurane 2 %, rocuronium
Early signs: EtCO₂ rising at the same ventilation, tachycardia
Established MH: hyperthermia, acidosis, rising potassium
Trigger off: sevoflurane stopped, O₂ 100 % at 10 L/min, ventilation 20 × 600
MH treatment under way
Dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg given
Cooling: 2 L saline at room temperature running
Calcium chloride 10 mg/kg and insulin 10 U with dextrose given
Sodium bicarbonate 1 mmol/kg given
Recovering: EtCO₂ below 45
Ventilation back to 12 × 500, O₂ 100 %
Cardiac arrest
CPR (defibrillate VF from the Devices tab)

Objectives
Name malignant hyperthermia from the monitor: EtCO₂ above 45 mmHg at the same ventilation, tachycardia (instructor-assessed)
Call the MH crisis (stop sevoflurane, O₂ 100 % at 10 L/min, hyperventilate) within 120 s of the early signs (EtCO₂ above 45 mmHg at the same ventilation)
Give dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg within 300 s of calling the crisis
Repeat dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg within 600 s of the first dose while EtCO₂ is still above 45 mmHg
Treat the potassium (calcium chloride, insulin with dextrose) within 300 s of K⁺ rising above 5.5 mmol/L
Hyperventilation kept until EtCO₂ has stayed below 40 mmHg for 2 min, then ventilation normalised (back to 12 × 500)
